profile.heroNoteHtml: Platform bets in AI, enterprise SaaS, and growth, taken from discovery to launch, with the numbers to prove it.

jobs.highlight: Modular agent platform scaled from 0 to 40+ enterprise customers
bullets: Cut AI use-case launch time from 14 weeks to 5 by modularising the AI agent (GXA) into reusable chunking, embedding, and access-flow components.
Pitched and shipped centralised SSO after discovery flagged sign-in friction as the top adoption blocker, unlocking $2M in incremental revenue.
Owned the AI roadmap for the Customer Data Platform, turning 30+ enterprise customer interviews into bets that lifted engagement 30% across 500K+ users.
Killed a fine-tuning track after evals showed retrieval drove 80% of failures, redirecting the squad to reranking and lifting containment from 20% to 41%.
Redesigned customer service routing across CRM, messaging, and knowledge-base surfaces, cutting manual ops 30% and resolution time from 3 weeks to 2 weeks.
Defined the consent, access-control, and audit-logging model for AI workflows, making the assistant sellable into FedRAMP and GDPR-bound enterprise accounts.

Built the AI quality framework tracking retrieval accuracy, deflection, and adoption with per-answer observability and human review on edge cases, the org's first shared definition of a working AI feature.
Grew ARR by $3M in a single quarter by running 12 A/B tests across onboarding and pricing, lifting signup-to-paid conversion 35%.
Shipped a conversational engagement product from concept to GA for 50K+ SMB customers, driving 30% more interactions and 15% less support volume.
Rebuilt PLG onboarding after 20+ discovery interviews, lifting activation and CSAT 60%.
Sequenced the roadmap across 3 squads, turning customer and sales signal into prioritised bets and cutting sprint carry-over 25%.

jobs.highlight: Lifted patient engagement 30% on regulated platform
bullets: Lifted patient engagement 30% and renewals 20% by scoping a patient monitoring product around third-party risk-scoring models.
Delivered 5 features across 2 squads in 6 months on a HIPAA-regulated stack, while addressing all audit findings on data governance.
Uncovered workflow gaps through discovery with care managers and payers across 3 accounts, resequencing the roadmap around real clinician needs.

jobs.highlight: WebEIM scheduling automation across 200+ utility accounts
bullets: Translated scheduler and dispatcher workflows on WebEIM (energy scheduling and imbalance-settlement automation for utilities) into roadmap input across 5 releases, lifting CSAT 50%.
Productised WebEIM onboarding into a standard configuration flow, shortening time-to-go-live 20% and support tickets 30%.
Translated compliance mandates into shippable roadmap scope for a regulated energy SaaS suite, across 3 engineering pods.
Accelerated delivery velocity 40% and time-to-ship 30% by moving a 30-person team from waterfall to Scrum.
Mined user behaviour data to surface content quality signals, formalised into guidelines adopted by a 200+ person org.

skills.heading: AI PM toolkit: how I actually build
skills.intro: I work like an AI PM, not a feature manager. Discovery with users, then evals, then ship. I decide what the model should do, what it must never do, and how we know it worked — with observability on every answer and a human in the loop where stakes demand it. The cards below are my real stack. Tap any card to see how I use it on real work.

items.title: Evals before models
items.description: I write the test before I touch the model. Golden sets, grounding checks, containment and accuracy — with observability on every answer and human review on edge cases. At Granicus this call moved containment from 20 to 41 percent with zero fine tuning.
items.more: Tap to see my eval loop +

modal.title: Evals before models: my loop
modal.intro: I start every AI task by writing down what good looks like. No golden set, no ship. At Granicus the team wanted fine tuning. Evals showed retrieval caused 80 percent of failures, so we fixed chunking and reranking instead. Containment went from 20 to 41 percent. My eval operating sheet shows the five dimensions, observability, the human-in-the-loop, and a field example.

steps.text: pull 200 past tickets, label the right answer and the source it must cite.
retrieval hit, grounding, refusal quality. One blended score hides the real break.
nothing ships below the bar. New misses become new evals.

steps.lead: Observe and keep humans in the loop
steps.text: every answer logs sources, confidence, and outcome; low-confidence and high-stakes answers queue for review, and each reviewed miss becomes a new eval.

items.title: Retrieval and grounding
items.description: Most wrong answers are retrieval misses, not model misses. I work chunking, embeddings, reranking and citations until the answer can prove where it came from.

modal.title: Retrieval and grounding: my method
modal.intro: Users forgive a bot that says it does not know. They never forgive a confident lie. So I treat retrieval as the product. Clean chunks, fresh embeddings, rerank, then force a citation in the answer.

steps.text: policy sized pieces with headings kept, so the answer quotes the real rule.
cheap recall, careful second pass, drop anything below threshold.
no source means no answer, just a clean handoff with context kept.

items.kicker: What the model must never do
items.title: Guardrails and safe UX
items.description: I design abstain and route flows, confidence thresholds and human review for edge cases. In regulated accounts a clean refusal beats a confident wrong answer.

modal.title: Guardrails and safe UX: the pattern
modal.intro: For regulated customers the refusal path is the feature. I set confidence bands: answer, ask one clarifying question, or refuse and route. Every refusal keeps full context so the human never starts cold.

steps.text: the model says what it will not do, states why, and hands off with full context.
low confidence answers route before sending; high-stakes categories always route, regardless of confidence.
consent, sources, confidence, and reviewer actions logged per answer for audit and weekly review.

items.title: Agents and platforms
items.description: I turn one-off demos into reusable pieces. At Granicus I split the agent into chunking, embedding and access flow parts, which cut launch time from 14 weeks to 5.

modal.title: Agents and platforms: the split
modal.intro: One-off bots do not scale. At Granicus I broke our agent into three reusable parts: how we split content, how we find it, and who is allowed to see it. New use cases then became assembly, not rebuilds. Launch time fell from 14 weeks to 5.

steps.text: one way to split and version content.
one way to embed, rerank and cite.
one way to check consent and permission before answering.

modal.result: New use cases assembled from the same base instead of rebuilt; launch time 14 weeks to 5.

items.title: Experimentation and analytics
items.description: I run growth like science. At Maropost 12 tests in a quarter added $3M ARR. Funnels, cohorts, SQL, and a log so we never retest a settled question.

modal.title: Experimentation and analytics: the playbook
modal.intro: At Maropost we ran 12 tests in a quarter and added 3M ARR. The trick was not more ideas, it was a shared log: hypothesis, metric, result, learning. Winners scaled, losers stayed dead.

steps.text: if everything changes, nothing learned.
activation, retention or revenue, picked before ship.
top 3 learnings shared, backlog reprioritised.

steps.text: SSO, provisioning, clean offboarding.
consent records, access checks, audit logs, residency options.
pilot tenant, admin docs, support script, rollback path.

teardowns.heading: Teardown: Intercom Fin, read as an outsider
teardowns.intro: A teardown of a product I do not own, in four parts. Each card opens the full breakdown: who it serves, where it breaks, what I would fix first and how I would measure it.

cards.title: 1. Problem and persona
paragraphs: Product: Intercom Fin, an AI support agent sold to B2B SaaS support teams. Read from public docs and behaviour, not insider knowledge.
Persona: support ops lead at a 500+ seat B2B SaaS, owns CSAT and handle time, fears wrong answers more than slow answers.

cards.title: 2. Journey and competition
paragraphs: Journey: ticket arrives to bot attempts answer to low confidence to human handoff to resolution logged to bot learns (or does not).
Competition: Zendesk AI optimises containment; Sierra and Decagon sell accuracy plus evals. My read: eval-gated answers with cited sources beat raw containment in regulated markets.

cards.title: 3. Differentiation and pricing
paragraphs: Differentiation: retrieval-grounded answers with confidence bands. Abstain-and-route beats confident-and-wrong where compliance matters.
Pricing: per-resolution pricing aligns cost with value; enterprise tier adds audit logs, residency, SSO.

ordered.text: block launch below containment + accuracy bars.

ordered.note: Metric: reopen rate, CSAT on bot conversations.

teardowns.outroHtml: Method only: this is an outside-in read of a third-party product. My own comparable AI support work is written up under Case studies. Want this lens on your product? Reach out and I will walk you through it.

modals.title: Intercom Fin: problem and persona
paragraphs: Problem: support teams drown in repeat tickets while users wait hours for simple answers. Bots promise relief but guess, and one wrong policy answer burns more trust than ten slow ones.
Persona: support ops lead at a 500 seat B2B SaaS. Owns CSAT and handle time. Fears wrong answers more than slow answers.
Scope note: observed from outside; where docs are silent I say so rather than invent internals.

modals.title: Intercom Fin: journey and competition
paragraphs: Flow: ticket arrives, bot tries, low confidence hands to human, resolution gets logged, bot should learn. Most bots skip the last step.
Competition: Intercom Fin and Zendesk AI push containment. Sierra and Decagon sell accuracy plus evals. My read: eval gated answers with cited sources beat raw containment in regulated markets.

modals.title: Intercom Fin: differentiation and pricing
paragraphs: Differentiation: grounded answers with confidence bands. Abstain and route beats confident and wrong where compliance matters.
Pricing: per resolution pricing fits value. Enterprise tier adds audit logs, residency and SSO. Pilot on low risk intents, expand only as evals pass.
